caption.text:
Save these summer spots in the city center for this weekend 🙌 

1. Farmers Market: On Saturdays from 6.00 to 12.00 you can find some fresh flowers, vegetables & fruits from the region and freshly baked bread at the market in Oerlikon. 
.
.
2. The Bagel Shop: Enjoy a delicious bagel and coffee to go from the new take away @thebagelshopzurich located in the city center! We tried the Pastrami Dreams and loved it 😍
.
.
3. Flussbad Oberer Letten: Swim, relax and enjoy the view at the Flussbad Oberer Letten💦 And treat yourself to a lunch or refreshing drink @gump_letten 
.
.
4. Haus am Fluss: Zurich’s newest hotspot! An oasis to escape the city, enjoy drinks, and savor meals with a view of the Limmat. @hausamfluss.zuerich 
.
.
5. Streetfood Festival: Don’t miss the fantastic street food at Turbinenplatz! We savored Mantu and a Pulled Beef Burger. 🌞 @streetfoodfestivalzurich 
.
.
6. Gerolds Garten: A late night drink @fraugeroldsgarten is always a good idea! We also checked out the talented surfers @urbansurf.zrh under the night sky! 
.
.
.

summary.title: We Are in the Making
summary.description:

Cover art by @parna_deshpande

node.text:
Uma homenagem a rede social que contribui muito para divulgação do meu trabalho.
.
O Instagram tem sido para mim muito mais que uma simples rede social; essa plataforma que além de criar uma conexão com pessoas que queremos por perto, tem ajudado assim como eu  milhões de pessoas a divulgar o seu negócio.
Essa poderosa Midia social, gerou milhares de empregos, e continua dando a oportunidade para todos os que desejam divulgar o que fazem de melhor.
.
.

A tribute to the social network that contributes a lot to spread my work. . For me, Instagram has been much more than just a social network; this platform that in addition to creating a connection with people we want close by, has helped millions of people to publicize their business just like me. This powerful social media has created thousands of jobs, and continues to provide an opportunity for everyone who wants to spread the word about what they do best. .
THANK YOU @instagram!

node.text:
Hoje é um dia muito importante para o @instagram, com a chegada do novo logo/ícone e novo layout do aplicativo. Eu estou extremamente honrado de participar desta mudança e de ter sido uma das pouquíssimas pessoas do mundo a vê-lo antes do anúncio oficial. Fui convidado por eles para recriar o novo logo, assim como fiz há cerca de 3 anos quando criei a hashtag #MyInstagramLogo. Nesse período, mais de 4.000 pessoas criaram suas próprias versões do logo anterior, de todas as formas possíveis. Essa mudança representa um novo começo para eles, por isso é um momento tão importante. Convido a todos que já participaram do #MyInstagramLogo a participarem novamente! 😊

Today is a very important day for @instagram, with the announcement of their new logo/icon and a brand new layout. I'm extremely honored for being part of this change and for being one of the very few people in the world to see it before the launch. I was invited by them to recreate their new logo, just like I did it before about 3 years ago when I created the #MyInstagramLogo hashtag. During this period, over 4.000 people have created their own version of the previous logo, in many different ways. This change represents a new fresh start for them, so that's why it's such an important moment. I invite you all that have been part of #MyInstagramLogo before to create your new version! 😊

caption.text:
Fernando Magalhães’ (@mglhs_com) ever-evolving futuristic beings live in the Genesis HumanProject.Alpha, a computer-generated world he dreamed up at the end of 2018. The London-based Brazilian artist uses procedural modeling, a programming technique that creates 3D models and textures.⁣
⁣
“I’m only able to see them [his characters] once the render is done — so it’s kind of like meeting somebody for the first time,” explains Fernando. “I love to see them and try to understand, to feel from where they came from, who they are, what they do and so on.”⁣
⁣
“Today I’m working in this universe that I created, but my mind goes much further than that. Through my work, I hope people understand that art goes beyond what we know as art, there’s different paths, approaches and possibilities.” #ThisWeekOnInstagram⁣
⁣
Digital images by @mglhs_com

“Laissez-nous rêver.” ✨💭✨

Let us dream. That’s the message of France’s @impulstar (Impulstar) Finale, which just celebrated its 11th year.

The annual street football event gives 14- to 16-year-olds from the suburbs the opportunity to have an audience of some of the country’s leading names in sports, music, dance and content, making way for those dreams to become a reality.

Join creators @mr_boris_becker (Boris Becker) and @jenybsg (Jeny Bonsenge) as they go head-to-head to see who should host. Then learn more and see highlights from the Impulstar Finale on today’s story. ⚽️ 💫

node.text:
“I know my nails are going to turn a little yellow after this — but the food is good.” ❤️💛 
 
Meet @maitreyiramakrishnan (Maitreyi Ramakrishnan), star of the @netflix series “Never Have I Ever.” To celebrate the premiere of season three, which explores experiences surrounding the South Asian diaspora, Maitreyi spent a day in NYC on an epic food tour. 
 
“This is a very heartwarming moment for me because everyone is appreciating food that I’ve grown up with my entire life,” says Maitreyi as she samples a dosa from a busy food cart. “This is Tamil pride right here. This makes me so happy. It’s not just people in the film industry, it’s all different industries in all different ways, and that to me is cultural appreciation — because that line is really diverse.” 
 
Follow Maitreyi as she tastes foods (and some very spicy spices 😂) from Sri Lanka, Nepal and Malaysia. 🔥❤️✨ 
 
Music by @tesherrrr

node.text:
#HelloWorld.

“My work is simply to be enjoyed. I considered it escapism, something to indulge in and forget about the bullsh*t.” Alec West’s (@alec.fbx) colorful lo-fi renderings throw back to gaming’s early years. “I make animations that mainly just capture a moment in an ever-growing world, each video being another piece in the puzzle. All my life I have been creating art. In middle school, I would go on websites and watch pivot stick fighter animations all day. I would attempt my own crude versions at home downloading pre-made assets.”

Alec developed his pixelated world and original character Tri-Tails using free open-source software. “The work that took a team of 40-plus people 20 years ago, I can do in my room alone today. I am excited to see where these tools will take us and what will be made. I am in a server with extremely talented artists, ranging across many different forms of digital art and software. I don’t know what I would do without this community. Having people to reach out to for help and just general questions is something I won’t ever take for granted. This is something anyone should be able to do if they want. It’s our goal to not only inspire but help them achieve that goal.”

Video by @alec.fbx
Music by @goreshit.sucks

node.text:
“I like to bottle up auras only I can see, in the hopes other people can see them too,” says Nat Ćmiel, the visual artist and musician who is manifesting the otherworldly, ethereal enigma that is yeule (@yeule).

“The yeule project is a sonic and visual time capsule that snapshots eras of my shape-shifting self and the experience of pathos. Musically, yeule lies somewhere between electronic nu-pop cy-earth music II and indie confessional emo.” Born in Singapore and based in London, the self-styled “glitch princess” was a quiet and introverted child before finding their sense of belonging online — drawing inspiration for yeule from the cyber dimension. “As a Singaporean artist, I feel proud of representing Southeast Asia in the electronic music scene. I stand for mental health awareness, trans rights and dedicate my work on this earth to the friends I lost, who couldn’t be seen the way they wanted to be.

I want to hit that spot where it hurts so bad and burns so hot, but you can never take a picture or show anyone what it looked like. Songwriting starts from the dreams and memories that scar the most and end up in my journal in crumpled pieces of paper. I hope it sounds pretty, even though the contents are decaying inside. I won’t sing something I don’t mean, and I don’t play something I don’t really like. There must be a reason why I chip at this concrete so meticulously, right? To make it look as close as it can to what I have seen with my own eyes.”

Video by @yeule

node.text:
Artist Jon Batiste (@jonbatiste) is a whole vibe. 🎶 He’s heading to the Grammy Awards (@recordingacademy) with 11 different nominations — the most of any nominee this year. 🤯👏

But before Jon’s performance at the awards, he met up with friends in New York City for one of his self-proclaimed “love riots.”

“Love riots are like chaotic, fun, impromptu musical parades. It started as something I would do in transit from one place to the next, whether on the way to the recording studio or to rehearsal or even just to the market,” says Jon. “It borrows from the second-line tradition of my hometown New Orleans, typically starting with a few people and gathering folks along the way. I love the feeling of ceremony and sense of community that it brings.”

Meet Jon’s community and hear his soulful sound from the subway to the studio before tonight’s show in Las Vegas.

🤍🏳️‍⚧️ “Growing up, I never really saw anyone who truly represented me in mainstream media. Trans Day of Visibility is important because it reminds trans people that they are not alone. There are so many people within our community who are making the world a better place. This day represents being bold and thriving in a world that is not always the most welcoming or safe for us.” —Writer and creator Devin Halbal (@devinhalbal)

Video by @devinhalbal

node.text:
🚨 Can we have your attention, please?

We're on set with Nigerian artist Omah Lay (@omah_lay) who teamed up with Justin Bieber (@justinbieber) for their new single, “Attention.”

“One thing I hope people take away from this song especially is the emotion, the realness,” says Omah, known for his Afro-fusion beats. “It’s always about me telling a story.”

node.text:
For ceramicist Lisa Asano (@lisa_asano), every new vessel is a new journey. The creation process, the final product and what happens to a piece once it’s in someone’s hands — every step along its way is one worth celebrating.

“Black joy to me is just the most contagious joy. I feel like it’s the most fulfilling and happiest joy that you could ever feel. I’m lucky to say that I’m able to experience that type of joy in my life.”

This Black History Month, we’re continuing to #ShareBlackStories and celebrate Black joy in all its glory.

Video by @lisa_asano

node.text:
Joy for Jordan Parker (@jpcharisma) means taking time for himself to do things he loves. Even better when that time is spent with butterflies. 🦋

“Every time you see them, they grab your attention,” says the butterfly gardener. “They’re just so elegant and so beautiful.”

This Black History Month, we’re continuing to #ShareBlackStories and celebrate Black joy in all its glory.

Circling in on the weekend with @allmyrescuedbirds.

Anfissa the rock pigeon was rescued by her human Amina, a licensed wildlife rehabber. “I rescue hundreds of birds every year,” says Amina. “I rehabilitate and release them, and disabled birds get adopted. Anfissa became my best pet.”

#WeeklyFluff

Video by @allmyrescuedbirds
Music by @kttunstall

node.text:
#HelloWorld

“My work captures worlds that I’d like to escape to.” —@cyborgypo (Kim)

“My work is a visualization of sounds, emotions, concepts and environments, all in the digital world that is cyborgypo. I started creating collages from my phone at home, and eventually I started collaging cool textures and images that were around me. The signature elements in my work are slimy and shiny stars, flattened or puffy. The recurring themes are memories, heartbreak and castles,” says Kim, who uses a combination of photos, 3D rendering, photo-editing tools and machine learning to create her art.

“It’s incredibly important to me to create pieces that can be interpreted as just being cute elements that are also something deep and meaningful. I want to communicate through my work what I’m feeling in that moment of creating it, whether that is joy or pain. Creating is a great tool for pleasure and healing.”

Art by @cyborgypo

node.text:
“My music is sexy, and so I am.” —Singer @amaarae (Amaarae)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Amaarae was born in NYC, then raised in Atlanta, Ghana and New Jersey.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“What I took from Atlanta was the heaviness of the drums and the love for horn lines and making that very gritty and hip-hop. In New Jersey, I heard Britney Spears’ ‘Blackout’ and I fell in love with the idea of pop not being cookie cutter, but being interesting and having an edge. And in Ghana, as far as African music goes, I think the inspiration is endless.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Fearlessness, sexiness and real love for danger and passion drives Amaarae’s music. “The beauty of matters of the heart” are the emotional core to her lyrics. “My songwriting reflects points in my life and my state of mind at the time. With ‘Fountain Baby,’ [her new release] I was dealing with a lot of extreme changes in my life and the fears and the risks that came with exploring that — and deciding whether I wanted to step into it. I was in an extremely confident place. I didn’t think I could fail. And I think that reflects a lot in the songwriting, too.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Photos of @amaarae by @naichamercier⁣⁣

node.text:
Wow. It’s time for @tik.tacocat’s (Taco) cardio.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“Taco started using the treadmill about four years ago. Now, it’s become a routine,” says his human, Victoria. “I turn it on for him as soon as I get home from work, and he’s figured out how to turn it off when he’s done!” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#WeeklyFluff⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Video by @tik.tacocat⁣⁣
Music by Handsome Dancer

node.text:
Brazilian singer @ludmilla (Ludmilla) made @tashaokereke & @tracieokereke’s (Tasha & Tracie) dreams come true with a DM. She reached out and asked the hip-hop duo (and twin sisters) to collaborate on the song “Sou Má” on her newest album.⁣
⁣
“When I sent them a DM, they were really happy, and I was even more so, because they also wanted it, and I really dig their music. It was a perfect match!” Turns out, the sisters had always wanted to work with Ludmilla. 💖⁣
⁣
#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.⁣
⁣
P.S. @beyonce, please check your DMs from Ludmilla. 🔥

⁣⁣

node.text:
@femalepentimento’s (Female Pentimento) magical, reorienting photo-based images explore nature, the metaphysical and diverse ways of inner healing. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“My hope is that the things I create convey a sense of divine beauty and sacredness, reminding us of the interconnectedness of all things,” says the nonbinary artist, whose aesthetic practice augments the immediacy of the captured image through layering, collage and digitally painting on top of photographs. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“The feminine spirit of nature, as the originator of life, holds a special place in my heart. I see my artistic process as a way of honoring this spirit and sharing its radiance with others. I’m interested in different natural phenomena — rainbows, sunlight, lightning. I love how symbolically loaded these elements are throughout cultures and art history. Light forms and light portals are probably one of the most magical elements I experiment with in my images. They border on the fantastical and imagine a world of what could be.” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Art by @femalepentimento

node.text:
“I and my approach to comedy are very go with the flow and organic. I never like to post anything that hasn’t already made me laugh before I posted it.” —Creator @isaiahxavier (Isaiah Xavier Howard) ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
“I’m a very big open book and I crave human connections, so I love to share myself with other people. The most common themes in my videos are dating, relationships, the LGBT community, being Black and the human experience as a whole. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I was destined to be funny, given the family I was born into. Humor was a major coping mechanism for all of us that I just naturally adopted, just to make everything a bit more lighthearted and easily digestible. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I am here to be the best version of myself I can be and encourage everyone else to be the best version of themselves, as well. My content is a reflection of me going through life, figuring everything out as I go and looking cute in the process.” ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Video by @isaiahxavier

🗺️Only a few demade cities left in Hoenn. Today we have Slateport, another coastal city that shares a lot of similarities with Lilycove City to the northeast.

Slateport and Lilycove have a lot in common. Both have a museum, ferry port, contest hall, and a large market. Despite those similarities, Slateport has always felt bigger and more vibrant to me. 

It could be because the beach on Route 109 to the south is filled with additional NPCs and acts as an extension to the already busy city. The commercial hub of the city is also much larger and is closer to a farmer’s market than the Lilycove department store. Their respective music themes do an excellent job at differentiating the two. Lilycove’s is more slow and relaxed, while Slateport’s fast, energetic and percussion heavy. 

It’s so cool that two same-sized cities that share a lot of the same landmarks feel so different from each other. What are your favorite story beats or memories from Slateport? Had you noticed how similar these two cities are before?

caption.text:
#HelloWorld

“My work captures worlds that I’d like to escape to.” —@cyborgypo (Kim)

“My work is a visualization of sounds, emotions, concepts and environments, all in the digital world that is cyborgypo. I started creating collages from my phone at home, and eventually I started collaging cool textures and images that were around me. The signature elements in my work are slimy and shiny stars, flattened or puffy. The recurring themes are memories, heartbreak and castles,” says Kim, who uses a combination of photos, 3D rendering, photo-editing tools and machine learning to create her art.

“It’s incredibly important to me to create pieces that can be interpreted as just being cute elements that are also something deep and meaningful. I want to communicate through my work what I’m feeling in that moment of creating it, whether that is joy or pain. Creating is a great tool for pleasure and healing.”

Art by @cyborgypo

“My music is sexy, and so I am.” —Singer @amaarae (Amaarae)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Amaarae was born in NYC, then raised in Atlanta, Ghana and New Jersey.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“What I took from Atlanta was the heaviness of the drums and the love for horn lines and making that very gritty and hip-hop. In New Jersey, I heard Britney Spears’ ‘Blackout’ and I fell in love with the idea of pop not being cookie cutter, but being interesting and having an edge. And in Ghana, as far as African music goes, I think the inspiration is endless.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Fearlessness, sexiness and real love for danger and passion drives Amaarae’s music. “The beauty of matters of the heart” are the emotional core to her lyrics. “My songwriting reflects points in my life and my state of mind at the time. With ‘Fountain Baby,’ [her new release] I was dealing with a lot of extreme changes in my life and the fears and the risks that came with exploring that — and deciding whether I wanted to step into it. I was in an extremely confident place. I didn’t think I could fail. And I think that reflects a lot in the songwriting, too.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Photos of @amaarae by @naichamercier⁣⁣

Wow. It’s time for @tik.tacocat’s (Taco) cardio.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“Taco started using the treadmill about four years ago. Now, it’s become a routine,” says his human, Victoria. “I turn it on for him as soon as I get home from work, and he’s figured out how to turn it off when he’s done!” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#WeeklyFluff⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Video by @tik.tacocat⁣⁣
Music by Handsome Dancer

caption.text:
Brazilian singer @ludmilla (Ludmilla) made @tashaokereke & @tracieokereke’s (Tasha & Tracie) dreams come true with a DM. She reached out and asked the hip-hop duo (and twin sisters) to collaborate on the song “Sou Má” on her newest album.⁣
⁣
“When I sent them a DM, they were really happy, and I was even more so, because they also wanted it, and I really dig their music. It was a perfect match!” Turns out, the sisters had always wanted to work with Ludmilla. 💖⁣
⁣
#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.⁣
⁣
P.S. @beyonce, please check your DMs from Ludmilla. 🔥

⁣⁣

caption.text:
@femalepentimento’s (Female Pentimento) magical, reorienting photo-based images explore nature, the metaphysical and diverse ways of inner healing. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“My hope is that the things I create convey a sense of divine beauty and sacredness, reminding us of the interconnectedness of all things,” says the nonbinary artist, whose aesthetic practice augments the immediacy of the captured image through layering, collage and digitally painting on top of photographs. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“The feminine spirit of nature, as the originator of life, holds a special place in my heart. I see my artistic process as a way of honoring this spirit and sharing its radiance with others. I’m interested in different natural phenomena — rainbows, sunlight, lightning. I love how symbolically loaded these elements are throughout cultures and art history. Light forms and light portals are probably one of the most magical elements I experiment with in my images. They border on the fantastical and imagine a world of what could be.” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Art by @femalepentimento

“I and my approach to comedy are very go with the flow and organic. I never like to post anything that hasn’t already made me laugh before I posted it.” —Creator @isaiahxavier (Isaiah Xavier Howard) ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
“I’m a very big open book and I crave human connections, so I love to share myself with other people. The most common themes in my videos are dating, relationships, the LGBT community, being Black and the human experience as a whole. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I was destined to be funny, given the family I was born into. Humor was a major coping mechanism for all of us that I just naturally adopted, just to make everything a bit more lighthearted and easily digestible. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I am here to be the best version of myself I can be and encourage everyone else to be the best version of themselves, as well. My content is a reflection of me going through life, figuring everything out as I go and looking cute in the process.” ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Video by @isaiahxavier

caption.text:
Home alone 🐾🐾🐾 ⁣
 ⁣
Left to his own devices on a rainy day with an open doggy door, @otis_thedoodle_olson (Otis Olson) got down and dirty. ⁣
 ⁣
“Otis is such a bouncy and happy dog who loves to play, snuggle and stir up trouble,” says his human, Alexandra. “He continues to love to dig and play in the rain, and our white couch is continuing to fight for its life.” ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @otis_thedoodle_olson

caption.text:
The @nba Finals tipoff today and @lethalshooter (Chris Matthews) is locked in. 🏀 🏆 🔒 ⁣
 ⁣
“Basketball got me to college and eventually overseas as a pro,” says Chris. “I was always known for my shooting, and after I retired from my professional career overseas, I realized I could transition to my next career as a shooting coach.” ⁣
 ⁣
When he’s not in the gym working with NBA players, you’ll find the Washington, D.C.-native shooting coach and content creator dreaming up his next hoops challenge. “I work with a welder who has been helping me bring these crazy ideas to life for the last two years. It’s a great outlet for creativity.” ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @lethalshooter

caption.text:
#HelloWorld ⁣
 ⁣
Multimedia digital artist @serotinesart’s (Serotines) celestial, iridescent post-human characters exist beyond the rules and expectations of “real life.” ⁣
 ⁣
“Part of digital art’s power is that it’s not constrained by things like physical space or materials. You can create anything, fuse different mediums together, find endless inspiration. ⁣
 ⁣
I switched from primarily 2D to 3D art. I found a drawing forum that had free digital art programs. Before that, I had uploaded my marker and pen drawings. After I tried digital art, I was hooked and started using a drawing tablet. I don’t know how to code yet, but I know how to model things and animate, so that’s my solution. ⁣
 ⁣
I usually start with a character design, and then the personality comes as I create more pieces of work featuring them. I see my angel characters as alternate forms of my human characters. It could be an interpretation for the way we have real-life and online identities? The bright, super rainbow colors are also prevalent; their artificial feeling really pushes the ‘beyond this world’ theme in my art.” ⁣
 ⁣
Art by @serotinesart 
Music by @jackolis_v

caption.text:
“Both me and my music are authentic versions of myself. There is no character or gimmick. No mask being worn. No trying to be somebody else.” —@jawnyutah (JAWNY)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
JAWNY’s eclectic sound bridges indie, alternative, rock, pop and funk. “My music is a reflection of me and my interests and all of the music I bumped elbows with and loved growing up on,” says the singer, songwriter and producer who refuses to let the success of his 2019 breakout, viral hit “Honeypie” define him. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“‘Honeypie’ was the greatest lesson I ever learned. I made something that I did not think super hard about and put it out into the world. It found people who connected to it. It was insane. I thought I had to make music like that again. While trying and failing at doing that, I learned the beauty of what that song is and was. It was me, in my studio, chasing an idea that got me excited. Whatever happened after that fact is extra. That is how I will always approach making music.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
My new record ‘It’s Never Fair, Always True’ walks through the entire process of falling in love, falling out of love and dealing with it in chronological order. The album ends exactly where it starts saying the same line, ‘It’s never fair, it’s always true,’ but in a completely different context than it was said in the intro.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Photos of @jawnyutah by @kevin_amato

caption.text:
Celebrate Cannes Film Festival with French creators @paolalct (Paola Locatelli) and @theodortytb (Theodort), who are experiencing the glamour of the French Riviera… assuming they make it in time and can stay awake! 
 
Here’s #10Things Cannes edition: 
 
1. Ready for an evening on the town.
2. Can(nes) Paola make it to the airport in time for her flight?
3. “You’re going to miss the film.” 😂💀
4. Paola taking in what all the French Riviera has to offer.
5. Theodort attended the premiere of “Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny.”
6. Oh, look! It’s @sundyjules.
7. Decisions… decisions…
8. That’s what friends are for.
9. The 🌟🌟 of Cannes at the @instagram Creators Night Out party.
10. Signs of a good time.

caption.text:
“My personal experience of seeking to be seen, heard and understood in a world where I felt incredibly alone is at the core of my current work on Asian American identity,” says Japanese-Taiwanese-American multidisciplinary artist, activist and nail tech @ameyaokamoto (Ameya Marie Okamoto). 
 
Ameya’s nail art explores Asian American visibility through themes like identity, status, exploitation and the impact of forced migration on body politics. “I started doing nails out of my dorm room last year. I was immediately obsessed with how nail art and service work connected to Asian American identity and my own immigration story. Most Asian immigrants, including my grandparents, came to America as service.” 
 
Ameya’s #GoingHomeAgainProject is a reckoning with Asian Americans’ forgotten history. “I am currently traveling across America via train visiting and memorializing sites across the U.S. that hold particular importance to the Asian American diaspora and fight for civil rights. 
 
It is important to me that my art complicates the idea of Asian America and helps educate young people about their hidden histories that they would otherwise not be taught in schools. When you don’t have a lot of examples of people who look like you, it’s hard to imagine who you might be able to become.” 
 
Photos by @ameyaokamoto @visualsbyalyvia and @mattdicksonphotography

@hallebailey (Halle Bailey) couldn’t believe it when @serenawilliams (Serena Williams) showed up in her DMs to say hi.❣️ 
 
“I was dying at the interaction and I didn’t know what to say! She’s an amazing sister. And I connect with her relationship with Venus and their amazing sister duo. My sister and I look up to her and her sister so much,” says the star of @disney’s “The Little Mermaid.” 
 
“My advice? Always send a DM. It might just get seen.” 
 
#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.

caption.text:
“I see myself as limitless.” ✨ 
 
In the past five years, @keion211 (Keion Kopper) went from being a poet to a painter to a coder — from selling art on the streets to showing at prestigious exhibits. And he’s just getting started. 
 
“When people think of Black people, sometimes they just put us into one box. But we all live very nonlinear lifestyles, so you can tell different stories through the same lens of being Black.” 
 
Those different stories tell a bigger one about the influence of Black culture on society. “More people should realize that the things you love to do and say and wear and walk and talk and how you listen to TV, music, down to how you move your body, how you show love, sometimes stems from Black people.” 
 
Throughout the year, hear from future makers honoring the legacies of those who came before them. 🖤 If you can, listen with sound on and hear Keion recite one of his poems. Created in collaboration with @winterbreeanne and @liviarosejohnson. 
 
Photos by @keion211, @1osaci and @a16zclf. Art by @keion211

caption.text:
Actress @annacathcart (Anna Cathcart) decided to shoot her shot and sent a DM to her absolute favorite artist, @jpsaxe (JP Saxe). ✨

“To have him actually see that and to meet through that was so special and very exciting to me,” says the @xokittynetflix star. “My advice? Just send the DM! Because it might just get seen.”

#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.

caption.text:
“I love that people think my objects are not real.” —Designer and 3D artist @marierohanaa (Rohan Mirza) 
 
Rohan’s real-life accessory and fashion designs mix angelic and cyberpunk aesthetics. “My creations are representations of evolved bodies, a projection of a utopia and what the future holds. I started 3D during 2021, and it was a revelation. My work was very organic at the beginning, and today I try to work with sharper, more robotic shapes. Claws have been my signature for a long time, but also accessories that are way too big. I love to work on body parts like fingers, ears, face, because it’s on these areas that you can directly see a kind of mutation on the body,” says Paris-based Rohan. His original but wearable clothes honor his utopian sci-fi vision without going into cosplay. 
 
“My main concept is to bring pieces to reality that we can only imagine digitally. You don’t have to have a classical background to do things. No matter where you come from, the tools we have today are powerful enough to make it work.” 
 
Photos and videos by @marierohanaa

caption.text:
Being part of @hallebailey’s (Halle Bailey) world is magic. ✨🧜🌊

“I feel like Ariel would be an Aries like me — she’s very fiery, passionate. She knows what she wants.”

The star of @disney’s “The Little Mermaid” recently performed “Part of Your World” live for the first time, while at Disneyland in California.

“What I learned from Ariel is learning to speak up for myself and to use my voice, and knowing that as a woman you can be comfortable in the skin that you’re in and use that power that you have to voice what you need.”

caption.text:
“Music is time travel. Music is alchemy. Music is what gives you and me a true window into each other’s lives and minds. Music will bring us closer together.” —@kraejiyaeji (Yaeji) 
 
Yaeji started as a DJ in the leftfield, electronic underground scene before producing. “It all started from dance music and making mashups and edits. Dance music taught me the phonetic and rhythmic nature of using my voice, and repetition; something that’s still in my music today. 
 
My lyrics flow with no rules, so I’m not sure how exactly they come to be, but I recognize that some things are more easily expressed in Korean than English,” says the self-taught Korean and American DJ, singer and songwriter. 
 
“Because I have the technical tools, I can express my way without compromising anything. Not compromising anything is key, because I need it to be real and truly me. That’s what I want to share with young people who listen to me: they can relate and feel heard and seen through my music.” 
 
Video and music by @kraejiyaeji

collector.description:
Circling in on the weekend with @allmyrescuedbirds.

Anfissa the rock pigeon was rescued by her human Amina, a licensed wildlife rehabber. “I rescue hundreds of birds every year,” says Amina. “I rehabilitate and release them, and disabled birds get adopted. Anfissa became my best pet.”

#WeeklyFluff

Video by @allmyrescuedbirds
Music by @kttunstall

✩ hijab tutorial ✩ 
 
#InTheMoment 🎶 
 
Video by @abqariyyahalilintar 
Music by @thuymusic

When the whole group is on the same vibe. 😎 
 
Tap the “Add Yours” sticker and show us who you vibe with. 
 
Video by @thewilliamsfam 
Music by @feid and @itsyoungmiko

#HelloWorld

“My work captures worlds that I’d like to escape to.” —@cyborgypo (Kim)

“My work is a visualization of sounds, emotions, concepts and environments, all in the digital world that is cyborgypo. I started creating collages from my phone at home, and eventually I started collaging cool textures and images that were around me. The signature elements in my work are slimy and shiny stars, flattened or puffy. The recurring themes are memories, heartbreak and castles,” says Kim, who uses a combination of photos, 3D rendering, photo-editing tools and machine learning to create her art.

“It’s incredibly important to me to create pieces that can be interpreted as just being cute elements that are also something deep and meaningful. I want to communicate through my work what I’m feeling in that moment of creating it, whether that is joy or pain. Creating is a great tool for pleasure and healing.”

Art by @cyborgypo

“My music is sexy, and so I am.” —Singer @amaarae (Amaarae)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Amaarae was born in NYC, then raised in Atlanta, Ghana and New Jersey.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“What I took from Atlanta was the heaviness of the drums and the love for horn lines and making that very gritty and hip-hop. In New Jersey, I heard Britney Spears’ ‘Blackout’ and I fell in love with the idea of pop not being cookie cutter, but being interesting and having an edge. And in Ghana, as far as African music goes, I think the inspiration is endless.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Fearlessness, sexiness and real love for danger and passion drives Amaarae’s music. “The beauty of matters of the heart” are the emotional core to her lyrics. “My songwriting reflects points in my life and my state of mind at the time. With ‘Fountain Baby,’ [her new release] I was dealing with a lot of extreme changes in my life and the fears and the risks that came with exploring that — and deciding whether I wanted to step into it. I was in an extremely confident place. I didn’t think I could fail. And I think that reflects a lot in the songwriting, too.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Photos of @amaarae by @naichamercier⁣⁣

Wow. It’s time for @tik.tacocat’s (Taco) cardio.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“Taco started using the treadmill about four years ago. Now, it’s become a routine,” says his human, Victoria. “I turn it on for him as soon as I get home from work, and he’s figured out how to turn it off when he’s done!” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#WeeklyFluff⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Video by @tik.tacocat⁣⁣
Music by Handsome Dancer

Brazilian singer @ludmilla (Ludmilla) made @tashaokereke & @tracieokereke’s (Tasha & Tracie) dreams come true with a DM. She reached out and asked the hip-hop duo (and twin sisters) to collaborate on the song “Sou Má” on her newest album.⁣
⁣
“When I sent them a DM, they were really happy, and I was even more so, because they also wanted it, and I really dig their music. It was a perfect match!” Turns out, the sisters had always wanted to work with Ludmilla. 💖⁣
⁣
#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.⁣
⁣
P.S. @beyonce, please check your DMs from Ludmilla. 🔥

⁣⁣

🫶🏽🏳️‍🌈 ⁣
⁣
#InTheMoment: ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @neilshibata

@femalepentimento’s (Female Pentimento) magical, reorienting photo-based images explore nature, the metaphysical and diverse ways of inner healing. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“My hope is that the things I create convey a sense of divine beauty and sacredness, reminding us of the interconnectedness of all things,” says the nonbinary artist, whose aesthetic practice augments the immediacy of the captured image through layering, collage and digitally painting on top of photographs. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“The feminine spirit of nature, as the originator of life, holds a special place in my heart. I see my artistic process as a way of honoring this spirit and sharing its radiance with others. I’m interested in different natural phenomena — rainbows, sunlight, lightning. I love how symbolically loaded these elements are throughout cultures and art history. Light forms and light portals are probably one of the most magical elements I experiment with in my images. They border on the fantastical and imagine a world of what could be.” ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Art by @femalepentimento

“I and my approach to comedy are very go with the flow and organic. I never like to post anything that hasn’t already made me laugh before I posted it.” —Creator @isaiahxavier (Isaiah Xavier Howard) ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
“I’m a very big open book and I crave human connections, so I love to share myself with other people. The most common themes in my videos are dating, relationships, the LGBT community, being Black and the human experience as a whole. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I was destined to be funny, given the family I was born into. Humor was a major coping mechanism for all of us that I just naturally adopted, just to make everything a bit more lighthearted and easily digestible. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
I am here to be the best version of myself I can be and encourage everyone else to be the best version of themselves, as well. My content is a reflection of me going through life, figuring everything out as I go and looking cute in the process.” ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Video by @isaiahxavier

Home alone 🐾🐾🐾 ⁣
 ⁣
Left to his own devices on a rainy day with an open doggy door, @otis_thedoodle_olson (Otis Olson) got down and dirty. ⁣
 ⁣
“Otis is such a bouncy and happy dog who loves to play, snuggle and stir up trouble,” says his human, Alexandra. “He continues to love to dig and play in the rain, and our white couch is continuing to fight for its life.” ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @otis_thedoodle_olson

The @nba Finals tipoff today and @lethalshooter (Chris Matthews) is locked in. 🏀 🏆 🔒 ⁣
 ⁣
“Basketball got me to college and eventually overseas as a pro,” says Chris. “I was always known for my shooting, and after I retired from my professional career overseas, I realized I could transition to my next career as a shooting coach.” ⁣
 ⁣
When he’s not in the gym working with NBA players, you’ll find the Washington, D.C.-native shooting coach and content creator dreaming up his next hoops challenge. “I work with a welder who has been helping me bring these crazy ideas to life for the last two years. It’s a great outlet for creativity.” ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @lethalshooter

Girlllll ⁣
 ⁣
#InTheMoment ⁣
 ⁣
Video by @ini_cash

#HelloWorld ⁣
 ⁣
Multimedia digital artist @serotinesart’s (Serotines) celestial, iridescent post-human characters exist beyond the rules and expectations of “real life.” ⁣
 ⁣
“Part of digital art’s power is that it’s not constrained by things like physical space or materials. You can create anything, fuse different mediums together, find endless inspiration. ⁣
 ⁣
I switched from primarily 2D to 3D art. I found a drawing forum that had free digital art programs. Before that, I had uploaded my marker and pen drawings. After I tried digital art, I was hooked and started using a drawing tablet. I don’t know how to code yet, but I know how to model things and animate, so that’s my solution. ⁣
 ⁣
I usually start with a character design, and then the personality comes as I create more pieces of work featuring them. I see my angel characters as alternate forms of my human characters. It could be an interpretation for the way we have real-life and online identities? The bright, super rainbow colors are also prevalent; their artificial feeling really pushes the ‘beyond this world’ theme in my art.” ⁣
 ⁣
Art by @serotinesart 
Music by @jackolis_v

“Both me and my music are authentic versions of myself. There is no character or gimmick. No mask being worn. No trying to be somebody else.” —@jawnyutah (JAWNY)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
JAWNY’s eclectic sound bridges indie, alternative, rock, pop and funk. “My music is a reflection of me and my interests and all of the music I bumped elbows with and loved growing up on,” says the singer, songwriter and producer who refuses to let the success of his 2019 breakout, viral hit “Honeypie” define him. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“‘Honeypie’ was the greatest lesson I ever learned. I made something that I did not think super hard about and put it out into the world. It found people who connected to it. It was insane. I thought I had to make music like that again. While trying and failing at doing that, I learned the beauty of what that song is and was. It was me, in my studio, chasing an idea that got me excited. Whatever happened after that fact is extra. That is how I will always approach making music.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
My new record ‘It’s Never Fair, Always True’ walks through the entire process of falling in love, falling out of love and dealing with it in chronological order. The album ends exactly where it starts saying the same line, ‘It’s never fair, it’s always true,’ but in a completely different context than it was said in the intro.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Photos of @jawnyutah by @kevin_amato

A-a-aye, ⁣
I’m on vacation, ☀️🎵 ⁣
Every single day 😉 ⁣
 ⁣
Lounge into the weekend with @_jelly_of_nelly_ (Nelly)
⁣

Celebrate Cannes Film Festival with French creators @paolalct (Paola Locatelli) and @theodortytb (Theodort), who are experiencing the glamour of the French Riviera… assuming they make it in time and can stay awake! 
 
Here’s #10Things Cannes edition:

“My personal experience of seeking to be seen, heard and understood in a world where I felt incredibly alone is at the core of my current work on Asian American identity,” says Japanese-Taiwanese-American multidisciplinary artist, activist and nail tech @ameyaokamoto (Ameya Marie Okamoto). 
 
Ameya’s nail art explores Asian American visibility through themes like identity, status, exploitation and the impact of forced migration on body politics. “I started doing nails out of my dorm room last year. I was immediately obsessed with how nail art and service work connected to Asian American identity and my own immigration story. Most Asian immigrants, including my grandparents, came to America as service.” 
 
Ameya’s #GoingHomeAgainProject is a reckoning with Asian Americans’ forgotten history. “I am currently traveling across America via train visiting and memorializing sites across the U.S. that hold particular importance to the Asian American diaspora and fight for civil rights. 
 
It is important to me that my art complicates the idea of Asian America and helps educate young people about their hidden histories that they would otherwise not be taught in schools. When you don’t have a lot of examples of people who look like you, it’s hard to imagine who you might be able to become.” 
 
Photos by @ameyaokamoto @visualsbyalyvia and @mattdicksonphotography

@hallebailey (Halle Bailey) couldn’t believe it when @serenawilliams (Serena Williams) showed up in her DMs to say hi.❣️ 
 
“I was dying at the interaction and I didn’t know what to say! She’s an amazing sister. And I connect with her relationship with Venus and their amazing sister duo. My sister and I look up to her and her sister so much,” says the star of @disney’s “The Little Mermaid.” 
 
“My advice? Always send a DM. It might just get seen.” 
 
#Seen is our new series all about what’s possible when you connect in DMs.

“I see myself as limitless.” ✨ 
 
In the past five years, @keion211 (Keion Kopper) went from being a poet to a painter to a coder — from selling art on the streets to showing at prestigious exhibits. And he’s just getting started. 
 
“When people think of Black people, sometimes they just put us into one box. But we all live very nonlinear lifestyles, so you can tell different stories through the same lens of being Black.” 
 
Those different stories tell a bigger one about the influence of Black culture on society. “More people should realize that the things you love to do and say and wear and walk and talk and how you listen to TV, music, down to how you move your body, how you show love, sometimes stems from Black people.” 
 
Throughout the year, hear from future makers honoring the legacies of those who came before them. 🖤 If you can, listen with sound on and hear Keion recite one of his poems. Created in collaboration with @winterbreeanne and @liviarosejohnson. 
 
Photos by @keion211, @1osaci and @a16zclf. Art by @keion211

“I love that people think my objects are not real.” —Designer and 3D artist @marierohanaa (Rohan Mirza) 
 
Rohan’s real-life accessory and fashion designs mix angelic and cyberpunk aesthetics. “My creations are representations of evolved bodies, a projection of a utopia and what the future holds. I started 3D during 2021, and it was a revelation. My work was very organic at the beginning, and today I try to work with sharper, more robotic shapes. Claws have been my signature for a long time, but also accessories that are way too big. I love to work on body parts like fingers, ears, face, because it’s on these areas that you can directly see a kind of mutation on the body,” says Paris-based Rohan. His original but wearable clothes honor his utopian sci-fi vision without going into cosplay. 
 
“My main concept is to bring pieces to reality that we can only imagine digitally. You don’t have to have a classical background to do things. No matter where you come from, the tools we have today are powerful enough to make it work.” 
 
Photos and videos by @marierohanaa

Being part of @hallebailey’s (Halle Bailey) world is magic. ✨🧜🌊

“I feel like Ariel would be an Aries like me — she’s very fiery, passionate. She knows what she wants.”

The star of @disney’s “The Little Mermaid” recently performed “Part of Your World” live for the first time, while at Disneyland in California.

“What I learned from Ariel is learning to speak up for myself and to use my voice, and knowing that as a woman you can be comfortable in the skin that you’re in and use that power that you have to voice what you need.”

“Music is time travel. Music is alchemy. Music is what gives you and me a true window into each other’s lives and minds. Music will bring us closer together.” —@kraejiyaeji (Yaeji) 
 
Yaeji started as a DJ in the leftfield, electronic underground scene before producing. “It all started from dance music and making mashups and edits. Dance music taught me the phonetic and rhythmic nature of using my voice, and repetition; something that’s still in my music today. 
 
My lyrics flow with no rules, so I’m not sure how exactly they come to be, but I recognize that some things are more easily expressed in Korean than English,” says the self-taught Korean and American DJ, singer and songwriter. 
 
“Because I have the technical tools, I can express my way without compromising anything. Not compromising anything is key, because I need it to be real and truly me. That’s what I want to share with young people who listen to me: they can relate and feel heard and seen through my music.” 
 
Video and music by @kraejiyaeji

@mhammed_kilito (M’hammed Kilito) wants you to see something important: “Before It’s Gone.” 
 
“I felt an urgent need to capture and share the story of oases and their inhabitants when I found out that these ecosystems, and the people who rely on them, are facing numerous challenges, including droughts, desertification, water scarcity and overuse of natural resources,” says the documentary photographer. 
 
His long-term project, which shows the intricate relationships between human activity and the natural environment in these vital regions, was included in this year’s @worldpressphoto regional winners. The recognition is significant for M’hammed as it was a previous @worldpressphoto exhibition that inspired him to pursue a career in photography. 
 
“My hope is to inspire viewers and decision-makers to appreciate and care for these remarkable and complex ecosystems and to take action to preserve them and inspire change for a sustainable future.” 
 
Photos by @mhammed_kilito

#HelloWorld 
 
Artist @idalissner (Ida Lissner) describes her work as “narrative through world-building.” 
 
“I draw on many references from mythology, folklore and other stories embedded in the way we see, relate and understand ourselves in nature and in the more-than-human world. 
 
I always had ideas of small magical worlds in my head, but I couldn’t find a way to embody them. I was introduced to CGI and 3D towards the very end of my studies. These digital tools allow me to create places that resemble the world we know and something new and unknown — a place where we can visualize alternative realities that somehow mimic an experienced past, a parallel world or an imagined future. 
 
It may seem paradoxical, but I hope that my work will somehow inspire people to spend less time in front of the screen. The dream is that my images invoke some kind of re-enchantment with nature, and that they work as a reminder of what we sometimes take for granted.” 
 
Art by @idalissner

“I always wanted to look like an anime character.” —@shyr0dent (J) 
 
Born and raised in Beijing, J is a nonbinary multidisciplinary artist who moved to the US 10 years ago. “My world view is frequently challenged and always changing. I am always exploring alternative ways to express myself. I never forget my roots and look back at the life I had before. When creating art, I love to give my own twist on the two worlds together and tell my stories that way.” 
 
J studied fashion before making 3D digital art. “I am into 90s and ‘00s Japanese fashion, cyber Goth, punk Goth, Harajuku, Gothic Lolita style and I’m a big fan of vintage rave wear that is very retro futuristic. I am not making clothes anymore, but I still love fashion deeply and show it in my digital work. All the characters I have created resemble me. I like to think of them as different versions of me, or my different personalities. I love spreading positive energy and love while showing the world that side of me through my work.” 
 
Photos by @shyr0dent and @howaboutmia; art and video by @shyr0dent

“I like making something that feels way in the past, yet light-years into the future.” —@gracesrealm (Grace Requejo) 
 
Grace’s monochromatic, kawaii-noir aesthetic is infused with highly stylized, cartoonish characters, inspired by feminist sci-fi, medieval fantasy, techno primitivism and dress-up games. 
 
“I think of my illustrations as stories from this world I’m creating, and my sculptures are the objects, tools and memorials that exist in the world itself,” says the Filipino-American artist, who mostly works in graphite and uses clay for little charms and frames. 
 
“Each of my characters carries an air of emotional complexity. When I feel a strange or complicated emotion, I’ll hold onto that, then unravel it through drawing. My characters also have an aspect of self-portraiture to them, as I am often infusing aspects of my identity. 
 
I’ve been exploring paper-making more, which allows me to get to the root of both my art practice and my identity. I use this fiber called abacá, which is a natural leaf fiber grown in the Philippines. I like that I can connect with that aspect of my culture through my art.” 
 
Art by @gracesrealm

“My motivation is to help and heal as many people as I can while healing myself in the process.” —@flowerkidmusic (Flynn Sant, aka flowerkid) 
 
Themes like mental health awareness, childhood trauma and day-to-day struggles runs through flowerkid’s lyrically fearless, fragile music. “I try to provide as much hope as I can to those who need it. These things and honest storytelling make my music uniquely mine,” says the Australia-based musician. 
 
“I socially transitioned when I was 17 and physically began to transition when I was 18. My vocal journey as an artist has been one of the hardest parts — experiencing dysphoria because I couldn’t go through hormonal treatment while I was performing last year. Although I experience these negative emotions sometimes, I still feel euphoric with the progress I’ve already made and that I’m able to present myself to the world in my true form. The most important part of my career is helping people, and a huge part of that for me is to represent to the LGBTQ+ community in any way that I can. 
 
As a trans man, I feel a responsibility to protect fellow trans kids and adults. I want us to be treated just like any other human. It’s important to be as honest and open as possible. In my experience, the honesty tends to help people the most.” 
 
Photo of @flowerkidmusic by @elli0tt 
Music by @flowerkidmusic

“Lyrics are the most important part of my music. I want people to focus on what I’m saying, not how well I can sing.” —Artist and songwriter @nemahsis (Nemahsis) 
 
“Being a Palestinian born and raised in Canada, there are traces of both the Arabic scale and the French pop that I grew up with. These two influences tend to blend in my sound. I always volunteer my identity as Palestinian, because being Muslim is obvious in my appearance wearing hijab, and many times it overpowers my existence. 
 
My younger self always had a difficult time emotionally connecting to Eurocentric pop stars writing about heartbreak. There’s so much privilege in heartbreak being the strongest pain you’ve endured. No one was writing about the experiences millions of hijabi women go through daily. I created a solution to a problem. 
 
I felt as though I couldn’t write popular music until I fulfilled the duties of honoring my younger self. So long as I tried my best to make a difference, I deserve to write fun music that more people can relate to. It’s heavy creating conceptually freeing music — sometimes I just want to write a song that doesn’t feel like a trauma dump. Honesty is all I strive for.” 
 
Photos by @nemahsis

#HelloWorld 
 
@ch4ch__’s (aaron) music and lo-fi 3D animations take inspiration from early 2000s video games and analog technology — the perfect fit for each other. 
 
“I've been making beats way longer than anything else, so when I started doing this 3D stuff, I had a ton of unreleased music that finally had a home. The fact that it had an animation now made it resurface to a new audience,” says aaron. 
 
“I always like a little bit of crunchiness in my stuff, whether it be music or 3D. The pixelated look reminds me of the games I grew up playing, but it also functions as a tool to cover up some imperfections in the modeling side of things. 
 
The thrift3d series involves me finding objects in the wild and modeling them in 3D. Being able to capture those memories and interests and turn it into art was one of the first times I felt my work truly reflected me and my life.” 
 
Video by @ch4ch__

This #EarthDay, we’re celebrating the planet with artist and activist @tolmeia (Tolmeia Gregory). 🌏💚💫⁣
⁣
“Climate change activism isn’t just about going greener. It’s about ensuring that we can continue to have happy and healthy lives and ensure our children also will. It’s about watching sunsets and playing games with friends and dancing. It’s about falling in love. It’s about living!⁣
⁣
It’s a lot easier to focus on what’s going wrong in front of us than to sit back and dream of what we want to happen next, but I see more people daring to do it. Imagining your ideal world is a very hopeful thing, which also makes it a very brave thing to do, too.”⁣
⁣
Video by @tolmeia

On today’s #WeeklyFluff we’re horsing around with @thehorsechapter (Harvey), a Belgian warmblood gelding. ⁣

It’s prom night in Atlanta. ❤️🔥 
 
@jenemarie_ (Jené Marie) is a high school senior, a majorette dancer and a pro when it comes to planning the perfect prom experience. 
 
“I will never forget how all my loved ones came out to support and celebrate my prom night and all that I’ve accomplished academically throughout my senior year,” she says. “The reaction on their face when I entered the room with my prom look on was one to remember and the energy was so contagious. It was a feeling I will never forget.”

✨ Ramadan Mubarak! ✨ 
 
Comedian @nadirah.p (Nadirah Pierre) shares what Ramadan means to her. 
 
“Growing up, there’s nothing I loved more than going to the masjid to eat and to pray. Even before I could fast I enjoyed being around people from my community, sharing a meal and having an amazing time. 
 
Ramadan is not your only chance to do good deeds but rather a chance for you to start. You have the rest of the year and the rest of your life to improve.” 
 
Share your own moments of everyday kindness with the hashtag #MonthOfGood. 

Reel by @nadirah.p

“People have memories of places and things that make their hearts ache when they look at them.” —Japanese artist @ancccoo (ancco)

ancco’s work is about the nostalgia everyone experiences. “Having always worked in 2D, I recently devoted myself to ceramics. I am so fascinated with 3D works, because they allow me to strongly feel the actual existence of a character. The figure standing there is engraved with an irreplaceable and precious memory — something that makes up who I am today. All humans change, but I don’t think the things that restore us and that we’ve liked since childhood change very much.

When you go back to your parents’ home, do you ever find the toys and stuffed animals you used to play with lying dusty in storage or in the back of a display cabinet? I want to create the kind of work that brings back the time spent and the feeling you get when you touch these objects you have always loved, even if you had forgotten about them.”

Photos and Videos by @ancccoo

River City Magnolias (@rivercitymagnolias), Richmond’s amateur synchronized swim team, is Pool Hopping this weekend in celebration of their ten year anniversary! This popular water ballet club is known for sharing its nostalgia for the spirit of synchronized swimming of yesteryear while celebrating the current energy of our RVA community. The group always promotes a joyful, healthy, and body-positive approach to fitness. The Magnolias encourage an environment of diversity, friendship, self confidence, and perseverance.

So grab your swimsuit on Saturday for the Pool Hop and swim with the Magnolias after their performance marking 10 Years of Joy! You can participate in the Pool Hop and learn some skills at Randolph Pool, Battery Park Pool, and Blackwell Pool. 

In addition, make sure to ask the Magnolias about their giveback efforts too. They just wrapped up a donation drive that resulted in the collection of over 200 swimsuits, towels, swim caps, goggles, and more for Richmond City Public Pools @rvaparksandrec!

✔️Konsystencja jest całkiem gęsta i ma ładny delikatny zapach wyczuwalny przez jakiś czas. 
✔️Olejku wystarczy dosłownie kropelka żeby rozprowadzić na długości włosów. Bardzo dobrze on zabezpiecza końcówki jak i chroni przed promieniem UV. 
✔️Olejek został kupiony przeze mnie w biedronce zawsze praktycznie jest dostępny i kosztuje koło 5 zł a do tego jest bardzo wydajny wystarczy na pare dobrych miesięcy.

💼 Let's unravel the intricacies of stocks and their impact on the economy. 

📚 Stock Basics:
-Stocks represent ownership in companies, granting shareholders a stake in their success and assets.
-Companies issue stocks to raise capital for expansion, innovation, and operational needs.
-Investors can purchase shares, becoming part owners and sharing in profits.

🚀 Economic Impact:
-Stocks play a vital role in economic growth, fueling businesses and driving job creation.
-When companies thrive, they reinvest profits, launch new ventures, and contribute to overall economic development.
-Stock markets provide a platform for investors to buy and sell shares, ensuring liquidity and efficient allocation of capital.

💡 Benefits for Investors:
-Investing in stocks offers potential long-term wealth accumulation and financial growth.
-Investors can earn returns through dividends (a portion of company profits) and capital gains (increases in stock value).
-Owning stocks allows individuals to participate in a company's growth and support industries shaping our future.

“Today, like the sky I am feeling a little blue”
-
Remember that most of what you see on social media is edited and curated in a way that often depicts a life that is desired rather than lived day in day out
-
This results sometimes in people comparing their own reality to that of others often leaving them feeling inadequate and depressed
-
Here’s a dose of my reality today
-
I’m not always on cloud 9 and today is one of those days. While it’s not ideal it’s part of life’s ups and downs and that makes it ok
-
Here’s how I deal with a day like today
-
My normal routines become harder to maintain, I expect that. I also expect that if I let them routines slide I will only feel worse, so holding onto them becomes a priority not a choice
-
Sitting around feeling sorry for myself is only going to make things worse so I utilise tasks that will soak up time that could be spent ruminating or wallowing in self pity
-
I have been going for walks everyday but decided today to take a book with me and read a couple of chapters while basking in the glorious weather you see in this picture. Not only does this help with my ghost like skin tone but the vitamin D my body will absorb is proven to help boost my mood and also help with my sleep
-
How I feel today was not how I felt yesterday and tomorrow may be different still. This blue feeling will pass and it’s important to remind myself of that every time my mood attempts to derail me
-
I will tonight write as I do every night about my day, including the ups and downs and use that as an opportunity to consolidate today’s experience so that when I wake tomorrow I am stronger for it and hopefully feeling a little less blue
-
Dare Gratefully ❤️

PHOTO OF THE DAY /

Bruno V. Roels
Palmerar d'Elx, 2018
Watercolour on overprinted silver gelatin paper 
50 x 40 cm (19 3/4 x 15 3/4 inches)
Unique •
• £ 2,600 framed including VAT of 20% where applicable
•
•
£ 200 + VAT for UK delivery •
• 
10% of all sales will be donated to Hospital Rooms, a charity bringing art and arts programmes to mental health facilities within the UK. •
• 
Inspired by the American conceptual artist John Baldessari, there is an underlying surrealist sensibility to much of Roels' practice. Bruno V. Roels employs a playful, tongue-in-cheek tone throughout his work, whilst challenging the characteristics that traditionally define a photographic practice. Wanting to move away from the 'tyranny of camera viewfinders' and a tradition of photography that is defined by the technology and materials used, Roels instead focuses on the act of printing, not with the goal of creating a perfect print, but instead presenting all prints created as equal. •
• 
ART FOR GOOD
10% of all Black Box Projects sales will be donated to Hospital Rooms, a London-based charity championing the healing power of art by commissioning world-class artists to create permanent site-specific art installations and art programmes for secure mental health facilities in the NHS service. •
•

Contact the gallery for more information or to purchase this work. We are available on DM or info@blackboxprojects.art
